messages:
anya: Quick follow-up on the allocator RFC — we need to pick an async offload placement policy for the next sprint. My proposal: hotness-aware placement with a small fast-path for pinned KV caches.

mike: Can you sketch the heuristic? hotness-aware = LRU by token stream recency? :thinking:

anya: Yeah, roughly. We measure per-allocation access frequency and prefer GPU placement for allocations with high sustained seq-access. For short-lived allocations we keep them on CPU and only async-copy when access crosses a threshold.

sam: Two quick concerns: fragmentation and page-fault tail latency. If we keep moving chunks around async, how do we avoid tiny free fragments on GPU causing OOM while plenty of total mem exists?

anya: Good point. Plan is twofold: 1) allocator-level splitting/coalescing on free, with background compaction that only runs when fragmentation metric > X. 2) prefer allocation bump for ephemeral allocations (stack-like) to avoid holes.

zara: Background compaction is heavy. Who triggers it and what's the SLO? We can’t block inference requests.

anya: It’s best-effort background worker with soft quotas. Compaction runs on a dedicated CPU thread and issues device-to-device copies via pinned staging buffers; if compaction would violate latency SLO we postpone. We also expose compaction pressure metric so RLAT can back off.

mike: What about using CUDA Unified Memory (UM) vs explicit async copies? UM simplifies migation but page-faults can spike tail latency. We probably want explicit control.

sam: Agreed. Prefer explicit pinned host staging + async cudaMemcpy for predictable latencies. For some large persistent weights we can use UM if customers accept relaxed SLOs.

anya: Also proposing an allocator interface change: expose hint bits on allocations: {prefer_gpu, cpu_stage_ok, shared_cache, lifetime_hint}. Scheduler can set these from routing policy.

zara: That helps. Where do we surface this in the runtime API? Per-request metadata or per-model config?

anya: Per-model config defaults + optional per-request overrides. E.g., embeddings backend sets prefer_gpu:true for model weights, and requester can set cpu_stage_ok for experimental routes.

mike: Need metrics to validate: eviction_rate, async_copy_latency_p50/95/99, compaction_time, frag_ratio (largest_free / total_free), allocation_failures_by_reason.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary tests queued: offload-placement-heuristic A/B (20% of v2 instances) scheduled for 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC.

sam: For the A/B harness, include synthetic workloads: long-seq, streaming-chat, and short-burst embed. Measure token-throughput, p99 latency, and GPU utilization. Also track copy bytes/sec between host/gpu.

anya: Implementation note: prefer using a slab allocator for small objects (kv-cache entries) and a buddy/segregated fit for larger tensors to reduce fragmentation. Slabs can be pinned on GPU with overflow to host.

mike: We should avoid forcing clients to change code. Keep new hints optional and default to current behavior. Also provide a compatibility mode that uses current allocator until migration is validated.

zara: UX: admin console should show compaction pressure and fragmentation heatmap per node + per-model hints. Ops need to be able to toggle aggressive compaction for maintenance windows.

sam: Edge-case: model rollouts where new version has larger KV entries. We might need pre-warm migration to avoid OOM on rollout. Async prefetch+pin staging can help but ensure prefetch respects tenant quotas.

anya: Agreed. Add a prewarm job that reserves staging buffers and drives async copies with backpressure if quota exceeded.

mike: Concern: pinned host memory can starve system if we over-allocate. Need global pinned budget and eviction policy for pinned staging buffers.

anya: We'll enforce cluster-level pinned_host_budget and LRU eviction for staging buffers. If budget exhausted, fall back to synchronous copies (slower) or deny prefetch.

zara: One more tradeoff: compaction frequency vs wear on NVMe (if we spill to SSD). Keep spill writes append-optimized and compact less often.

sam: For now, prefer no-SSD spill in default config; enable spillonly in enterprise/private deployments where they accept different SLOs.

mike: Sounds actionable. Next steps: 1) prototype allocator + hint bits (PR), 2) implement metrics + dashboard hooks, 3) A/B canary with synthetic harness, 4) run compaction experiments.

anya: I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with the design and a minimal implementation plan. Assigning tasks in the PR. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident-bot: Note: no incidents linked to this thread.
